drafted_from: tool:google-account-delete_draft's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Delete my draft r-7301442210 for good. Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-delete_draft as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Delete my draft r-7301442210 for good." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-delete_draft, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"draft_id":"r-7301442210"}.
3. Read what comes back: the request goes as DELETE  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/drafts/r-7301442210.
4. Run tool:google-account-list_drafts to get the id; deleting a draft cannot be undone.

worked_examples.title: Delete a Gmail draft on a sample input
worked_examples.ask: Delete my draft r-7301442210 for good.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (its invoke url, method and body_template) and checked against tools/read-and-write-gmail/test/rows.test.mjs. A saved draft with id r-7301442210, as list_drafts gives it. The call it makes: DELETE the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/drafts/r-7301442210.
worked_examples.hands_back: Gmail answers with an empty body (the output has no fields), and the draft no longer appears in list_drafts. Deleting is permanent.
